Question Choices: Fill: A mother is 3 times as old as her son. In 10 years, she will be twice his age. How old is the son now?
Solution: x is the son’s current age and y the mother’s. Both advance 10 years. System: y=3 × x; y+10=2 × (x+10). Isolate y: y=(3)x+(0). Substitute into the other equation: (-2)x+(1)[(3)x+(0)]=10. Combine: (1)x=10, so x=10. Then y=(3)(10)+(0)=30. Check both equations: -3(10)+1(30)=0; -2(10)+1(30)=10. Requested answer: 10.

Question Choices: Fill: A person is 4 years older than twice their friend. Together they are 43 years old. How old is the friend?
Solution: x is the friend’s age; y is the other person’s age. System: y=2 × x+4; x+y=43. Isolate y: y=(2)x+(4). Substitute into the other equation: (1)x+(1)[(2)x+(4)]=43. Combine: (3)x=39, so x=13. Then y=(2)(13)+(4)=30. Check both equations: -2(13)+1(30)=4; 1(13)+1(30)=43. Requested answer: 13.

Question Choices: Fill: A cyclist rides up a route and returns down the same route, traveling uphill at 4 km/h and downhill at 12 km/h. Total travel time is 2 hours. Find the one-way distance in km.
Solution: x is the common distance traveled each way; add both travel times. x/4+x/12=2. The coefficient of x is 1/3, so x=6 km. Substitute this distance into BOTH time terms to recover the stated total. Requested answer: 6.

Question Choices: Fill: A system describes train and car times. Train: $t = 4h + 10$. Car: $t = 4h + 16$. How many solutions does this system have? (Type 0, 1, or Infinite)
Hints: Use equivalent line equations: identical lines, distinct parallel lines, or one intersection.
Solution: In standard form the first equation has coefficients (-4,1) and right side 10. Multiplying it by 1 gives coefficients (-4,1) and right side 10. The second has the same left side and right side 16. The constants disagree: a contradiction, so zero solutions. Requested answer: 0.

Question Choices: Fill: A container has small and large crates. A small uses 2 units and a large uses 5. 12 crates use 39 units total. How many large crates are there?
Solution: x is the small-crate count and y the large-crate count. System: x+y=12; 2 × x+5 × y=39. Multiply equation 1 by 5 and equation 2 by -1, then add to cancel y: (3)x=21, so x=7. Substitute back to obtain y=5. Check both equations: 1(7)+1(5)=12; 2(7)+5(5)=39. Requested answer: 5.
